---
title: "Appendix 1. Method reference"
author: "Mingyang Lu"
---

This appendix maps each computational task in the book to its R and Python
implementation and to the chapter where it is developed. The idea behind a method is
language-agnostic, so the two implementation columns are meant to be read side by
side: pick the language you work in, and use the other column to translate.

**How to read the tables.** A name in `monospace` is a function *defined from scratch
in the book* (the method is built up so you understand it, not called as a black box).
A name written as `package::function` or as a library (for example `scipy.integrate`)
is a standard library used where it is the practical choice. The R and Python
implementations use parallel function names throughout, so a homemade function usually
appears under the same name in both columns; where a name differs (or where one
language uses a library and the other does not), the columns show it. The libraries
themselves are collected in [Appendix 2](appendix-library-map.qmd).

```{=html}
<style>
/* Keep the wide reference tables inside the content column: a table wider than the
   column scrolls horizontally within it instead of overflowing the page. */
main table.table { display: block; overflow-x: auto; font-size: 0.85rem; }
main table.table td, main table.table th { vertical-align: top; }
</style>
```
